description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

The transcript credits Dr. Harry Coover with developing cyanoacrylate-based adhesive (later known as super glue), originally tied to work on a gun sight and later a heat-resistant canopy. It then explains how, in Vietnam, medics used super glue when other options weren’t available to bind wounds, helping prevent bleeding and keeping casualties alive until they could reach more advanced medical care. It also notes the transcript’s cautions: it wasn’t officially recommended because it lacked FDA approval for wound treatment, and side effects could include contamination and skin irritation. What other “improvised medicine” should we cover next?
